$comment: The machine-readable form of the only end-to-end reading this project has. Every number here is quoted from docs/01-product-whitepaper.md §2.3, which reports four runs of the adopted arm configuration against the same judge. It exists so that an acceptance gate reads a number instead of a paragraph, and so that a document and a gate cannot disagree about what was measured.
reader: DeepSeek, adopted arm configuration (user turns only, 48,000-character window)
judge: the official per-category LongMemEval judge prompts
metric: judge accuracy, mean of four runs
classificationCaveat: The category denominators here are 150 / 72 / 30 / 121 / 127. The published LongMemEval splits are 150 information-extraction (70 user + 56 assistant + 24 preference variants counted differently), 78 knowledge-update, 133 multi-session and 133 temporal-reasoning across the same 500 questions. The cleaned local copy regroups thirty of them, so a category percentage in this file is not directly comparable with a category percentage quoted from a paper that used the published grouping. This is recorded rather than corrected because changing the grouping now would move eleven historical readings at once.
abstentionCaveat: The thirty false-premise questions form their own bucket rather than being counted inside their parent category, so the five rows sum to 500 (150 + 72 + 30 + 121 + 127). A published paper that keeps them inside the parent category will report different category percentages on the same questions.
